Short onboarding that reuses KYC data already on file.
Full capture flow when nothing is on file yet (mobile, PIN, ID, selfie, prepaid card).
Portfolio value, holdings, unrealized P&L, live buy/sell price at a glance.
1D/1W/1M/3M/1Y price history, DB-backed for the daily ranges with a local fallback.
Buy by grams or by EGP, in 0.1g steps, with a price-locked order summary and PIN confirmation.
Sell by grams or by EGP, proceeds credited to the Aman prepaid balance.
Holdings, asset allocation, today's realized P&L, cumulative realized P&L chart.
Calendar and bar views of realized P&L per day.
List of past orders and a detail view with before/after balances.
Customer info, KYC status, linked payment method, documents, FAQ.
Spread, fee, limits, quote validity, funding method — one config, never hardcoded in UI.
getCurrentGoldPrice / getHistoricalGoldPrices / getBuyPrice / getSellPrice behind one interface, swappable for a real provider.

Insufficient balance, insufficient gold, price changed, failed transaction, provider unavailable, KYC incomplete, market volatility.

PRD, business flow, architecture, assumptions/compliance/risk/roadmap.

Event tracking and a KPI dashboard for acquisition, activation, engagement, transactions, financial, risk metrics — not built at all.

Summary: Price engine behind a swappable interface
Description:
As a engineering team, I want to call getCurrentGoldPrice / getHistoricalGoldPrices / getBuyPrice / getSellPrice without knowing whether the data is mocked or real, so that a real provider can replace the mock later without touching the UI.

Acceptance criteria:
- Given the UI needs a price, when it calls the pricing service, then it never imports the mock provider directly.
- Given the Supabase gold-price-history table is reachable, when historical prices are requested, then real data is used; when it is not reachable, then a local static fallback is used silently, with no error shown to the customer.

Notes: Verified: services/pricing.ts, services/history.ts, services/supabase.ts

Summary: Cash and gold balances are always derived from the ledger
Description:
As a engineering team, I want to never store a cash or gold balance separately from the transaction history, so that the balance can never drift out of sync with what actually happened.

Acceptance criteria:
- Given any sequence of buys and sells, when I independently recompute cash and gold from the transaction list, then it matches what the UI shows, exactly.
- Given two orders are submitted in rapid succession, when they process, then they are serialized (one at a time), never applied concurrently against stale state.

Notes: This is the fix for DEF-01/02/03 (duplicate orders, balance drift, oversold gold) — see delivery-pack Defects sheet for the original bugs.

As a reviewer / QA, I want to trigger insufficient balance, insufficient gold, price-changed, failed-transaction, provider-unavailable, KYC-incomplete, and volatility states on demand, so that I can verify the app handles failure gracefully, not just the happy path.

Acceptance criteria:
- Given I use the Prototype controls panel, when I toggle any of the 7 states, then the corresponding screen shows the correct message and blocks the action it should block.

Notes: Verified: components/PhoneShell.tsx controls + corresponding checks in services/engine.ts

As a designer / engineer, I want to a component library with named tokens (not just Tailwind utility classes) and documented usage, so that new screens stay visually consistent without someone remembering the exact hex codes and spacing by heart.

Acceptance criteria:

Description:
As a engineering team, I want to capture a signature as a canvas the customer draws on with finger or mouse, reusable across any flow that needs consent evidence, so that onboarding and future consent flows don't each reinvent signature capture.

Acceptance criteria:
- Given a screen renders the signature pad, when the customer draws a stroke, then the pad reports a captured signature and shows a 'Captured' status; when they tap Clear, then it reports null and reverts to 'Required'.
- Given the pad has no stroke yet, when the surrounding step is evaluated, then any Continue/Submit button gated on it stays disabled.

Notes: Verified: components/ui.tsx (SignaturePad). Client-side only, not persisted to the store, consistent with the other simulated-capture steps (ID photo, selfie).

Summary: Brand-new customer signs to authorize their eKYC declaration
Description:
As a brand-new customer, I want to review a summary of what was captured (ID, selfie match) and sign to confirm it's accurate, so that my onboarding produces real evidence of consent, not just a captured photo nobody signed off on.

Acceptance criteria:
- Given I've captured my ID and selfie, when I reach the eKYC signature step, then I see a summary card (name, masked national ID, ID-captured status, selfie-match status) above the signature pad.
- Given the pad is empty, when I try to continue, then Continue is disabled; given I draw a signature, when I tap Continue, then I proceed to the prepaid-card step.

Notes: Verified end-to-end in browser: OnboardingNew.tsx step 8 of 11. Positioned after ID + selfie capture, before card issuance.

Summary: Existing customer signs to authorize adding Gold Investment
Description:
As a existing Aman customer new to Gold, I want to sign to authorize enrolling in the Gold product, since my core identity KYC is already on file, so that Aman has consent evidence for this specific product, without repeating identity verification I've already done.

Acceptance criteria:
- Given I check 'I have read and agree to the terms', when the checkbox is ticked, then a signature pad appears labeled for authorizing Gold Investment.
- Given the signature pad is empty, when I try to tap Start Investing, then it's disabled; given I sign, when I tap Start Investing, then onboarding completes.

Notes: Verified end-to-end in browser: Onboarding.tsx (OnboardingExisting) step 6. Lighter than E21-S2 since identity eKYC is not repeated for existing customers.
